newsitem.title: USA: Inland Steel union contract offer approved.
newsitem.headline: Inland Steel union contract offer approved.

text.p: Inland Steel Industries Inc. said Tuesday its contract offer for the United Steelworkers of America has been approved by an arbitrator.
The contract covers some 7,000 employees at the Indiana Harbour Works in East Chicago and the Minorca Mine in Virginia, Minn. It followed a five-day arbitration hearing last month.
The contract covers the second half of a six-year agreement with the steelworkers, which runs through July 31, 1999. The company and the union had agreed to reopen the contract in mid-term.
The two did not reach a settlement on their own, so as agreed each submitted a final offer to an arbitrator, who chose Inland Steel's, the company said.

Steelworkers at Inland will receive wage increases of 50 cents an hour retroactive to Aug. 1, and an additional 25 cents a hour on Aug. 1, 1997 and Aug. 1, 1998, the company said. In addition, lump sums of $1,000 will be paid in each of the three contract years, and workers will receive one additional holiday and increased retirement benefits.
Inland Steel's stock rose 12.5 cents to $18 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
